core.m1: An apartment is a rented room or unit inside a larger building.
core.m2: Many newcomers start out renting an apartment.
core.e1: I rented a small apartment downtown.
core.e2: Is this apartment available next month?

core.m1: A house is a standalone building, often with its own yard.
core.m2: Houses usually cost more than apartments.
core.e1: We are looking for a house to rent.
core.e2: This house has a big backyard.
core.p1: We are looking for a _______ to rent.

core.m1: A condo is a privately owned unit inside a shared building.
core.m2: Condos often include a gym or pool.
core.e1: She bought a condo near the subway.
core.e2: This condo has a nice view.
core.p1: She bought a _______ near the subway.

core.m1: A basement suite is a rental unit below the main floor of a house.
core.m2: It is often cheaper than the upper floors.
core.e1: We live in a basement suite.
core.e2: The basement suite has its own entrance.

core.m1: A roommate is someone you share a home with.
core.m2: Splitting rent with a roommate saves money.
core.e1: My roommate pays half the rent.
core.e2: I'm looking for a roommate.

core.m1: A lease is a written agreement between you and the landlord.
core.m2: Read it carefully before you sign.
core.e1: I signed a one-year lease.
core.e2: Please review the lease before signing.

core.m1: A landlord is the person who owns and rents out the property.
core.m2: Contact your landlord for repairs.
core.e1: My landlord fixed the heater quickly.
core.e2: I need to call my landlord.

core.m1: A tenant is a person who rents and lives in a property.
core.m2: Tenants have certain legal rights.
core.e1: As a tenant, you must pay rent on time.
core.e2: The tenant reported a leak.
core.p1: As a _______, you must pay rent on time.

core.m1: A security deposit is money paid before moving in, refunded if there is no damage.
core.m2: It usually equals one month's rent.
core.e1: I paid a security deposit last week.
core.e2: Will I get my security deposit back?

core.m1: Utilities are services like electricity, water, and gas.
core.m2: Ask if utilities are included in the rent.

core.m1: A bed is furniture used for sleeping.
core.m2: A new bed can be expensive.

core.m2: It's nice to know your neighbor's name.

core.m2: This neighborhood is quiet and safe.

extended.m: A studio apartment has one open room for living and sleeping.
extended.ex: Studio apartments are usually the cheapest option.

extended.m: A townhouse shares walls with neighboring homes but has its own entrance.
extended.ex: We rented a townhouse with a small yard.

extended.m: Furnished means the unit already includes furniture.
extended.ex: A furnished apartment saved us money.

extended.m: Unfurnished means you must bring or buy your own furniture.
extended.ex: We chose an unfurnished apartment to save on rent.

extended.m: A sublet is when a tenant rents their unit to someone else temporarily.
extended.ex: She found a sublet for the summer.

extended.m: A vacancy is an available unit for rent.
extended.ex: There is one vacancy left in the building.

extended.m: A co-signer agrees to pay rent if the tenant cannot.
extended.ex: New immigrants sometimes need a co-signer.

extended.m: A notice period is how far in advance you must inform your landlord before moving out.
extended.ex: The notice period here is one month.

extended.m: A renewal extends your lease for another term.
extended.ex: We signed a renewal for one more year.

extended.m: Eviction is when a landlord legally forces a tenant to leave.
extended.ex: Late rent can sometimes lead to eviction.

extended.m: A rental application is a form landlords use to screen tenants.
extended.ex: I submitted my rental application yesterday.

extended.m: A credit check reviews your financial history before approving a lease.
extended.ex: The landlord ran a credit check.

extended.m: A nightstand is a small table beside the bed.
extended.ex: I put a lamp on the nightstand.

extended.m: A dresser stores folded clothes in drawers.
extended.ex: My clothes are in the dresser.

extended.m: A bookshelf holds books and other items.
extended.ex: The bookshelf is almost full.

extended.m: Curtains cover windows for privacy and light control.
extended.ex: We hung new curtains in the bedroom.

extended.m: A lamp provides light in a room.
extended.ex: This lamp is too dim to read by.

extended.m: A washing machine cleans your clothes.
extended.ex: The washing machine is in the basement.

extended.m: An apartment complex is a group of buildings with many rental units.
extended.ex: The apartment complex has a shared laundry room.

extended.m: A bus route is the path a public bus follows.
extended.ex: Check the bus route before choosing a neighborhood.

extended.m: A park is a public green space for relaxing or exercising.
extended.ex: There's a park two blocks away.

extended.m: A community center offers local programs and activities.
extended.ex: The community center has free classes.

extended.m: Safety refers to how secure a neighborhood feels.
extended.ex: We chose this area for its safety.

extended.m: Walkability describes how easy it is to walk to nearby places.
extended.ex: This neighborhood has great walkability.

extended.m: A heating bill charges for warming your home in winter.
extended.ex: The heating bill is high in January.

extended.m: A gas bill charges for natural gas used for heating or cooking.
extended.ex: We split the gas bill evenly.

extended.m: A cable bill charges for television service.
extended.ex: We canceled our cable bill and use streaming instead.

extended.m: Automatic payment takes bill money from your account on a set date.
extended.ex: I set up automatic payment for my rent.

extended.m: A due date is the deadline for paying a bill.
extended.ex: The rent due date is the first of the month.

extended.m: A late fee is an extra charge for paying after the due date.
extended.ex: I paid a late fee last month by mistake.

phrases.note: Ask this when calling about a rental listing.

phrases.en: Are utilities included in the rent?
phrases.note: Always confirm this before signing a lease.
Ask this to plan your move.

phrases.en: Could you fix the heater, please?
phrases.note: Use this to politely request a repair from your landlord.

phrases.en: I'd like to renew my lease.
phrases.note: Say this before your lease term ends.

dialogues.title: Calling About an Apartment
dialogues.sit: You call a landlord about an apartment listing.
lines: Hi, is this apartment still available?
Yes, it is. Would you like to see it?
Yes, please. Are utilities included in the rent?
You can move in next month.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about a two-bedroom apartment instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice asking key rental questions on the phone.

dialogues.title: Viewing the Apartment
dialogues.sit: You visit the apartment in person with the landlord.
lines: This is the living room and kitchen.
It looks nice. Is it furnished?
That's fine. How much is the security deposit?
Great, here is the rental application.
Thank you, I'll fill it out today.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask if the apartment allows pets.
dialogues.tn: Practice asking follow-up questions during a viewing.

dialogues.title: A Maintenance Problem
dialogues.sit: Something in your rental unit is broken.
lines: Hi, could you fix the heater, please?
What seems to be the problem?
I'm sorry to hear that. I'll send someone tomorrow.
Thank you. Is there anything I should do tonight?
Use extra blankets, and I'll call you with the schedule.
dialogues.tp: Try again: report a broken refrigerator instead.
dialogues.tn: Problem scenario: report an issue politely and ask for next steps.

dialogues.title: Signing the Lease
dialogues.sit: You are ready to sign your lease agreement.
lines: Here is the lease. Please read it carefully.
Okay. What is the notice period?
Sign here, and print your name below.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about the renewal process instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice asking about lease terms before signing.

dialogues.title: Meeting a New Neighbor
dialogues.sit: You meet your neighbor for the first time after moving in.
lines: Hi, I just moved in. I'm your new neighbor.
Welcome! It's nice to meet you.
Is there a grocery store nearby?
Yes, it's just two blocks away.
Let me know if you need anything.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about the nearest park instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice friendly small talk when meeting neighbors.

speaking.q: What questions should you ask before renting an apartment?
speaking.h: You should ask if utilities are included and when you can move in.

speaking.q: Do you prefer a furnished or unfurnished apartment?
What should you do if something breaks in your rental?
speaking.h: You should contact your landlord and describe the problem.

speaking.q: Why is it important to read a lease carefully?
speaking.h: It's important because it explains your rights and responsibilities.

speaking.q: Describe the steps of finding and moving into a new apartment.
speaking.h: First you search for listings, then...

culture.title: Reading a Lease Carefully
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated tenant and landlord reviewing a lease document together at a table.
culture.notes: In Canada, a lease is a legal document, and tenants have specific rights. It is common and expected to ask questions before signing, and you can request time to review it at home first.
qs: Why is it acceptable to ask questions before signing a lease?
What information does a lease usually include?
What should you do if you don't understand a clause?

culture.title: Neighborhoods Can Feel Very Different
culture.tz: 每個社區的氛圍都不同
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated street view comparing a quiet suburban street and a busy downtown block.
culture.notes: Rent, safety, and walkability can vary a lot between neighborhoods, even in the same city. It's worth visiting an area at different times of day before deciding to rent there.
qs: What factors make a neighborhood convenient for daily life?
Why might visiting at different times of day help?
What is one tradeoff between downtown and suburban living?

words.tip: Curl your tongue back without touching the roof of your mouth.
Keep /l/ and /r/ clearly different in the same word.
Tap the tongue lightly for /r/, don't substitute /l/.
Practice each /r/ separately before saying the full word.
Touch the tip of your tongue to the ridge behind your teeth for /l/.

pronunciation.tip: Many Chinese speakers mix up /r/ and /l/. Practice minimal pairs like 'rent' vs 'lent' slowly.
pronunciation.prac: The landlord in this neighborhood rents a furnished apartment near the refrigerator repair shop.
